children: Colombia could adopt a tax incentive model similar to one used in Argentina to attract large-scale investments in energy and mining, Deputy Energy Minister Armando Cuello said on Wednesday.

Speaking at an economic conference in Bogota, Cuello said Colombia is studying whether to replicate aspects of Argentina's Incentive Regime for Large Investments, known as RIGI, which offers tax, customs and foreign-exchange benefits to major projects.
The scheme was introduced in 2024 under Argentine President Javier Milei.
"There is political will to create an environment that will bring back investment, which I know is a long-term endeavor," Cuello said.

After taking office in August, Colombian President Abelardo De La Espriella said his government would resume signing new hydrocarbon exploration contracts and allow fracking, reversing a ban imposed under former President Gustavo Petro.

Cuello said the lack of new project development under the previous administration had pushed Colombia's energy sector into crisis. He added that the country's power deficit had widened to 8.6% from 7.2% a week earlier.
He also said the government was taking all possible steps to avoid widespread power shortages during the El Niño weather phenomenon affecting much of Latin America.
